segment: The three scripts that the review forbade to run are repaired and their behaviour is verified on synthetic copies; none of them was run against the live data

merge-preserved-user-data.py.was: the target's state.db-wal and state.db-shm were deleted before the target database was read; the source was copied with a plain file copy, which loses whatever the source's write-ahead log still holds; the target was read with immutable=1, which ignores the log; the file trees were merged with copytree(dirs_exist_ok=True), which silently replaces newer target data with the older copy
merge-preserved-user-data.py.now: the session store is copied through the SQLite backup API with the source opened in ordinary mode, so every committed transaction is transferred; the source's own sidecars are read with the database and never removed; the target's sidecars are never deleted before the target database is read, and a read error is a refusal; the trees are merged with an explicit rule: a differing target file is KEPT and reported, only a missing one is copied
merge-preserved-user-data.py.verified: on synthetic copies: a row that exists only in the source's write-ahead log is transferred by the fixed path and lost by a plain file copy; the source's sidecars survive; the target's sidecars survive; a newer target file with the same name is not replaced

reprepare-ordinary-areas.py.was: the access store was emptied with an empty users map, which drops the generations and the tombstones the advance_access contract keeps; the existing first-preparation archive was deleted with rmtree before the next transfer
reprepare-ordinary-areas.py.now: the access store is not emptied at all: the script reports the rows before and after and lets the product's own preparation add the new generation while the previous ones stay as tombstones; the archive is never deleted: each transfer gets its own directory and a name collision is a refusal before any data changes
reprepare-ordinary-areas.py.not_run: the script was repaired but NOT executed: the serving home's areas are active and the transfer would change live data that is not needed for the live check

clear-access-tombstones.py.was: the script popped the principal's row out of the access document and wrote it back, destroying the access history, and it existed only to enable a fresh preparation
clear-access-tombstones.py.now: the script only reports: the principal's row, its generation, its enabled state, the store's tombstones and generations. Nothing is written. Removing an access row is a product decision of the product's own access transaction, not of an operator script

live_state_untouched.no_transfer_repeated: the transfer that was already executed is not repeated
